findings.title: deleteCache mutation never invalidates connectedCalendars query, leaving stale cache status in the UI
findings.body: The `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop. Unlike `disconnectMutation` (which invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in `onSettled`), nothing refetches the connected calendars query after the cache rows are deleted. `cacheUpdatedAt` comes from that query, so after a successful deletion the dropdown continues to show "Cache Status / Last updated: ..." and the "Delete cached data" item until the page is reloaded. In `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` `onChanged` is an optional prop that is frequently undefined, so the fallback does not help. Add `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` in `onSettled`/`onSuccess` of the delete-cache mutation.

findings.title: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds reports expired cache rows as live cache status
findings.body: The `groupBy` has no `expiresAt: { gte: now }` filter, whereas every read path (`getCachedAvailability`) only serves rows whose `expiresAt` is in the future. A credential whose cache entries have all expired (e.g. the Google watch channel lapsed a month ago) will still be shown in the UI as having a cache with a "Last updated" timestamp and a "Delete cached data" action, even though no cache is actually being served. This defeats the purpose of a cache status indicator. Filter on `expiresAt >= new Date()` (or return both values so the UI can show expired state).

findings.title: Access-denied/not-found case throws a plain Error, surfacing as a 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR
findings.body: When the credential does not belong to the caller (or does not exist) the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. tRPC maps non-`TRPCError` exceptions to `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR`, so a legitimate authorization failure is reported to the client as a server error (and will be logged/alerted as one). Use `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" })` or `"FORBIDDEN"` as the rest of the viewer routers do.

findings.title: Extra bulk UPDATE on every webhook refresh writes a field nothing reads
findings.body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` is invoked from the Google webhook handler on every push notification. The new `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` issues an `UPDATE SelectedCalendar ... WHERE credentialId = ?` solely to bump `@updatedAt` across all selected calendars for that credential (including event-type-level rows). The PR description itself notes the frontend does not consume `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` and uses `CalendarCache.updatedAt` instead. This is a redundant write amplifying webhook load with no consumer, and an empty `data: {}` relies on Prisma's implicit `@updatedAt` behaviour for `updateMany`, which is non-obvious to future readers. Remove it (or document the consumer if one is intended).

findings.title: `sed -i ''` is BSD/macOS-only syntax; script fails on Linux
findings.body: `sed -i '' -E "s|...|...|" "$ENV_FILE"` uses the BSD form of in-place editing. On GNU sed (Linux, which is what most contributors and CI use) `-i ''` is parsed as `-i` with no suffix followed by `''` as the sed script and `-E` as a filename, producing `sed: can't read -E: No such file or directory` and leaving `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` unchanged. Use a portable approach (e.g. `sed -i.bak ... && rm "$ENV_FILE.bak"`, or detect the platform).

findings.title: ENV_FILE is resolved relative to the caller's cwd, not the script location
findings.body: `ENV_FILE="../.env"` assumes the script is executed from inside `scripts/`. Running it the conventional way from the repo root (`./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`) resolves to a `.env` one directory *above* the repository; the script then prints a warning, `touch`es a stray file outside the repo and writes `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` there, so the app never picks it up. Resolve relative to the script: `ENV_FILE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)/.env"`. Additionally, `cleanup` always `exit 0`, so the failure paths (rate limit hit, URL not extracted) report success to the caller.

findings.title: Cache timestamp is hard-coded to the en-US locale
findings.body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` ignores the user's locale even though the surrounding strings are translated via `useLocale`. Non-English users will see a US-formatted date (M/D/YY, 12-hour clock) inside a localized sentence. `useLocale()` exposes the current locale (and the codebase already has dayjs/timeFormat helpers) — use it instead of the literal.

findings.title: UserWithCalendars now requires `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` on selected calendars although neither is used
findings.body: The `Pick<SelectedCalendar, ...>` for `allSelectedCalendars`/`userLevelSelectedCalendars` was widened to require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`, but nothing in this file (or in `connectedCalendars.handler.ts`) reads those fields — the UI gets its timestamp from `CalendarCache.updatedAt`. This tightens the public input type of `getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb`, which is re-exported for `@calcom/platform-libraries`/API v2, so any caller that builds the user object with an explicit `select` of only `externalId/integration/eventTypeId` will now fail type-checking for no functional benefit. Either drop the additions or actually use them.

findings.title: Migration header contradicts the statement and legacy rows will show the migration time as 'last updated'
findings.body: The header comment says the column is added "without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty", but the statement right below adds it with `DEFAULT NOW()`, so the warning is stale/misleading. More importantly, every pre-existing `CalendarCache` row is stamped with the migration run time, so after deploy the new UI will display "Last updated: <deploy time>" for all legacy caches regardless of how old their contents actually are. Consider back-filling from a meaningful value (e.g. `expiresAt - interval '30 days'`, which mirrors `CACHING_TIME`) or fix the comment to explain the inaccuracy.

findings.title: CalendarCacheRepository is instantiated directly, bypassing the calendar-cache feature flag
findings.body: Elsewhere the repository is obtained through `CalendarCache.init(...)`, which returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when the `calendar-cache` feature is disabled. Here `new CalendarCacheRepository()` is used unconditionally, so every `connectedCalendars` query performs an extra `groupBy` on `CalendarCache` and may surface stale cache status for deployments/teams that have the feature turned off (the mock, which this PR also updated, is never reached from this path).

findings.title: `dev:cron` switched to `npx tsx` but `tsx` is not a declared dependency
findings.body: The script now runs `npx tsx cron-tester.ts` while `tsx` is not listed in `dependencies`/`devDependencies` (only `ts-node` is). `npx` will try to download the latest `tsx` at invocation time, which is non-reproducible, fails offline, and bypasses yarn's lockfile. Either add `tsx` as a devDependency and call it directly, or keep `ts-node`. This change is also unrelated to the PR's stated scope.

findings.title: No tests for the new deleteCache handler or getCacheStatusByCredentialIds
findings.body: The PR adds a destructive mutation with an ownership check and a new repository aggregation, but no unit/integration tests: there is nothing asserting that a user cannot delete another user's cache, that the cache rows are actually removed, or that `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` returns the max `updatedAt` per credential. The PR description itself notes local verification was not possible. At minimum add handler tests for the forbidden/success paths and a repository test for the groupBy mapping.
